subject: science
title: Living or Not Living?
about: What every living thing does (grows, needs water, air and food or light, makes more of its kind, responds to the world) and sorting things that are living from things that only look alive or only move: a mushroom, an ant and a worm versus a cloud, a river, a ball and a toy robot (LS.1.1.1). Knowing what counts as living is the ground under NC's basic-needs objective.
tip: Point at things on a walk and ask the four questions: does it grow, does it need water, can it have babies, does it react when you get close?

cards.q: A puppy gets bigger every month. What is the puppy doing?
Which clue tells you a thing is living?
cards.note: Living things grow, need water, air and food or light, and make more of their kind.

cards.q: What needs water to stay alive?
cards.note: Every living thing needs water. A rock and a spoon do not.
Animals breathe air. Plants need air too, in their own way.
Living things make more of their own kind. A cat has kittens.

cards.q: A sunflower makes seeds. What do the seeds grow into?
cards.note: Plants make more of their own kind with seeds.

cards.q: You gently touch it and it wiggles away. What is it?
cards.note: Living things respond to touch, light, heat and sound.

cards.q: A dog hears a loud noise and jumps. What is the dog doing?
cards.note: Living things respond to what is around them. A rock never jumps.

cards.q: Which one grows, so it must be living?
cards.note: A mushroom grows, so it is living, even though it is not a plant or an animal.
Even tiny ants grow, eat and make more ants.
A toy looks like an animal, but it never grows, eats or breathes.

cards.q: Which one is a living thing?
cards.note: People are living things, just like animals and plants.

cards.q: Look up at the sky. Which one up there is nonliving?
cards.sayQ: Look up at the sky. Which one up there is non-living?
cards.note: A cloud moves, but it does not grow, eat or have babies. The wind moves it.

cards.q: Which one is a nonliving thing?
cards.sayQ: Which one is a non-living thing?
cards.note: A ball only moves when something pushes or pulls it.
A toy robot moves only with batteries. It never grows, so it is nonliving.

cards.q: A river moves fast and splashes. Why is it still nonliving?
cards.sayQ: A river moves fast and splashes. Why is it still non-living?
cards.note: Moving is not enough. Living things grow and need food or light.
A bike only moves when someone pushes or pedals it. It is nonliving.
